overview: After 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 f5 White develops 3.Nc3 and plays Nxe5 ideas if Black takes on e4. Black opens the f-file with ...fxe4 and goes for ...Qf6 or ...Nf6, accepting a loosened king for activity. Strong players do not trust it and White tends to keep a lasting advantage.

white_ideas.idea: Capture e5 with the knight and hit the Black king
Develop with d3 or d4 and keep a safe extra pawn

black_ideas.idea: Open the f-file with ...fxe4 and develop with ...Qf6 or ...Nf6
Use traps against careless White play

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with the e- and f-files open and an exposed Black king

gambit.notes: Black gives up central material for open lines and White can keep it with accurate play.

soundness.notes: Strong players consider the Latvian unsound; it scores through surprise.

structure.notes: Open: central pawns come off and pieces fight on open lines.

approach.notes: Seldom played by strong players, chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Tactics and refutations of traps; a dubious gambit is not a beginner choice.

character.reason: Forcing tactical play with an exposed king.

gambit.reason: Black gives material for activity; the anchor treats the Latvian as a Black gambit.

soundness.reason: The Latvian is a classic dubious gambit.

structure.reason: The e- and f-files open immediately.

approach.reason: The Latvian is an anchor offbeat opening.

plans.reason: Black brings the queen out early for activity.
